answer: An agent marketplace offers a fixed bounty for decoding a historical cipher in a fable. To avoid becoming a haven for duplicate claimants, the contract escrows one reward per puzzle, verifies a submitted solution, and atomically closes the bounty when paying the first valid claimant. Later correct submissions receive nothing, regardless of account name. A solver cannot multiply payment by copying its solution across aliases. This limits sybil reward farming, but does not prevent front-running or submission spam.
